content:
Want to use Signal on multiple devices at the same time? This encrypted messaging service now makes it easier for users to use the app across platforms between iPhones and other devices.

Signal users can now link another iPhone to their existing Signal account, rather than being limited to using only an iPad as a companion mobile device.

The company also announced support for Android linking today, stating: "We are expanding the linked devices feature on iOS so you can link an iPhone to your Signal account, and our support for iPad will continue."

When linking another iPhone, users can choose whether to transfer their full message history, as well as media files stored within the past 45 days.

Signal says the transfer process uses the same "link-and-sync" technology used for iPads and desktop devices (including Signal for Mac), with end-to-end encryption used throughout.

This expanded feature is particularly useful for users who need to keep their work and personal iPhones separate, as well as for those who need to test multiple devices.

Today's change also brings Signal's multi-device experience closer to Apple's Messages ecosystem, allowing seamless conversations between iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

Signal iOS version 8.22 is now available on the App Store. Signal has also previously rolled out a username feature, allowing users to contact each other without sharing phone numbers.
